main_text.l: abfurdius? fic omnes electi obediendo
fperi-nunt confilium Dei. o. At per vocem (præ-
cisè) vult Deum modo pendulo intendere
vel obedientiam, si obedierint, vel
non obedientiam, si non obedierint, & fic vel
gloriam justitiæ, vel misericordiæ intendit
Deus. Sed quæro cur Deus utrumque finem
indeterminatè proponat? Nempe
quoniam videt se alterutrum determinatè (ut ita
dicam) non affecuturum: at si hoc vi-
det, conjicit & divinat, fore fortasse ut
non obediat, ideoque ex scientiâ saltem
conjecturali scit, se finem non affecuturum, ergo
non intendit finem ex non præscientiâ 10.
Si ignorat intentum finem, quod est blasphemum,
quare sub disjunctione contrarios
fines intendit? Hic capiantur necesse est:
Deus enim sic præcisè intenderit unum fi-
nem, nisi de ipsius affecutione dubitaret, si
vero non dubitat, non potest utrum libet, sub
disjunctione sibi proponere. 11. Deum
fluctuare inter duos fines contrarios
est absurdum: nam ipsius voluntas est infinita
& à nullâ creaturâ determinata. Aquinas.
Si (inquit) præparatio ad gratiam, consideretur

page.notes: The left margin notes are small and partly set against the lines; their placement beside the text is approximate. The marginal marks "Aquin. 22" and "q. 112. art. 3" are read as one note, and "praedest. e 13. f. 5." is uncertain at its abbreviations. The running head is in small capitals and its last word is doubtful: it may read "FINEM" with a ligature. The "o." before "At per vocem" is printed and not a Roman numeral; it may be a sidenote marker. The first word "abfurdius?" carries the printed question mark and continues from the previous page. The last line "&Gre-" is a hyphenated break carried into the next page.
